President Trump has apparently taken charge of this year’s Fourth of July celebration in Washington, D.C., and will possibly give a personal address, angering some Democrats who fear the president will politicize the holiday.

City officials in the nation's capital were notified of Trump’s plan to address the nation on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial and move the traditional fireworks display from the Capitol Reflecting Pool to the nearby West Potomac Park, the Washington Post reported.

But the plans, which the administration says will allow more people to attend, have raised logistical concerns among officials as they make preparations for the holiday, which is fast approaching.

“We have a lot of people come to the Fourth of July. Logistically, over the years, the kinks have been worked out,” Mayor Muriel Bowser told the Post. “We don’t want to throw off what already works.”

The move to amend the July 4 celebrations in Washington comes after Trump floated the possibility of holding a military parade, an idea he got when he attended Bastille Day celebrations in France.

But the military parade idea was dropped after senior White House and Pentagon leaders estimated it would cost $92 million.

“When asked to give us a price for holding a great celebratory military parade, they wanted a number so ridiculously high that I cancelled it. Never let someone hold you up!” Trump tweeted.

Trump’s plans are being criticized not only for imposing a burden on the city logistically, but also for political reasons.

Rep. Betty McCollum, a Minnesota Democrat who chairs the House Subcommittee on Interior, Environment and Related Agencies, told the newspaper that Trump’s address would undermine the spirit of the celebration.

“It’s not about any one president. It’s about how our nation came to be, because of a hardy band of brave men and women,” she said.

“It’s not about any one person, it’s about ‘We, the people.’ And if the president moves to make this about him, I think he will find the America public disappointed and angered by it.”

I think it's safe to say that we're winning the war on information. I'm extremely grateful for these online communities who have fought this war from the onset and continue to do so. There will always continue to be a need for these communities to expose the truth and break the demoralized condition of the indoctrinated.

Victories in the Information War have united our spirits online however leaves us deeply divided in the real world. We are all afraid of throwing ourselves out there too far and the consequences for those we love. To this day I have only ever met one person I would proudly call "awake" which is never going to be enough to change this world for the better. It begs the questions to me of what's next to come? How will we know when it's time? How many of us are really out there? Would you feel ready if you met 100 of us in real life? 1000? 10000?

I've been trying to think of a safe way to show our beliefs and I think symbolically may be the best answer. If you think of the Christian Cross as an example it evokes powerful responses in people in many different ways. Ultimately it comes down to your belief about these symbols and the associations you can draw to them. This is no different to the crescent moon, the star of david, the E from Enron or the g from freemasonry. Symbolism is critical in promoting religions, ideologies and even corporations as it consolidates all knowledge.

Naturally for many here the swastika is the symbolic representation of our cause but I don't think it;s wise to use. The amount of energy and disinformation that has done into demonizing that symbol is too powerful to overcome.

Likewise the black sun which is another visually pleasing and powerful symbol as been linked to two incidents that have their share of controversies (Charlottesville and Christchurch). Despite your beliefs about what exactly transpired and why the symbol has now been tainted and can easily be demonized as a symbol of "white supremacy" or terrorism.

If we were to find a symbol that represents our values and see it represented in our day to day lives it will remind us that we are not alone. As it gains popularity for the right reasons we'll start to gain momentum. As we gain momentum we will eventually reach socially accepted prominence and the change we will all desire will occur with relative ease.

There's really three things that have to be decided when selecting a symbol for our cause:

 

  1. What the symbol stands for.
  2. What the symbol is.
  3. How the symbol is communicated/displayed.

 

I don't attest to know the answers to these questions but I'm interested to hear other's thoughts on the power and potential of symbolism.
